test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 06 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: When x is added to each of 20, 34, 11 and 16, then the numbers so obtained, in this order, are in proportion. Then, if 3x : y :: y : (2x-6), and y > 0, what is the value of y?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find **x** for **proportion** (a, b, c, d): x = (ad − bc) ÷ (b + c − a − d)

x = (20 × 16 − 34 × 11) ÷ (34 + 11 − 20 − 16) = (320 − 374) ÷ (45 − 36) = −54 ÷ 9 = −6

Substitute **x = −6** in **3x : y :: y : (2x − 6)** ⇒ y² = 3x(2x − 6) = 3(−6)(2(−6) − 6) = −18 × −18 = 324

**y = √324 = 18** (since y > 0)

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2261f5f1b4da8094cedc60af88782d6aa03285b3daa1e7d2459c0a61151cc688.png] 

**Given:** Numbers (20+x), (34+x), (11+x), (16+x) are in **proportion**.

**Formula Used:** a/b = c/d and y² = ac if a : y :: y : c

⇒ (20 + x) ÷ (34 + x) = (11 + x) ÷ (16 + x)

⇒ (20 + x)(16 + x) = (11 + x)(34 + x)

⇒ 320 + 20x + 16x + x² = 374 + 11x + 34x + x²

⇒ 320 + 36x = 374 + 45x

⇒ 45x − 36x = 320 − 374

⇒ 9x = −54 ⇒ **x = −6**

⇒ Now, 3x : y :: y : (2x − 6)

⇒ y² = 3x × (2x − 6)

⇒ y² = 3(−6) × (2(−6) − 6) = −18 × (−12 − 6) = −18 × −18

⇒ y² = 324 ⇒ y = √324 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

If b is the mean proportional between a and c, then a : b :: b : c, which implies **b² = ac**.

Basic Proportion Rule

Four numbers a, b, c, d are in proportion if **a × d = b × c** (Product of extremes = Product of means).

Third Proportional

In the proportion a : b :: b : c, the term **c** is called the third proportional to a and b, where **c = b²/a**.</p
